In 1996, Gore became involved in a ["Chinagate" campaign finance controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_United_States_campaign_finance_controversy "1996 United States campaign finance controversy") over his attendance at an event at the [Buddhist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhist "Buddhist")[Hsi Lai Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hsi_Lai_Temple "Hsi Lai Temple") in [Hacienda Heights, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacienda_Heights,_California "Hacienda Heights, California").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-biosen-32) In an interview on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC")'s _[Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today\_(NBC\_program) "Today (NBC program)")_ the following year, Gore said, "I did not know that it was a fund-raiser. I knew it was a political event, and I knew there were finance people that were going to be present, and so that alone should have told me, 'This is inappropriate and this is a mistake; don't do this.' And I take responsibility for that. It was a mistake."[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-CNNtemple-107) A U.S. Department of Justice investigation into the fund-raising activities had uncovered evidence that [Chinese agents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_intelligence_activity_abroad "Chinese intelligence activity abroad") sought to direct contributions from foreign sources to the [Democratic National Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Committee "Democratic National Committee") (DNC) before the [1996 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_United_States_presidential_election "1996 United States presidential election"). The [Chinese embassy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embassy_of_China_in_Washington,_D.C. "Embassy of China in Washington, D.C.") in Washington, D.C. was used for coordinating contributions to the DNC.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-108)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-109) FBI agents were denied the opportunity to ask President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore questions during Justice Department interviews in 1997 and 1998 and were allowed only to take notes.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-110)

In March 1997, Gore had to explain phone calls which he made to solicit funds for Democratic Party for the 1996 election.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-CNNcalls-111) In a news conference, Gore stated that, "all calls that I made were charged to the Democratic National Committee. I was advised there was nothing wrong with that. My counsel tells me there is no controlling legal authority that says that is any violation of any law."[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-PBSmoney-112) The phrase "no controlling legal authority" was criticized by columnist [Charles Krauthammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Krauthammer "Charles Krauthammer"), who stated: "Whatever other legacies Al Gore leaves behind between now and retirement, he forever bequeaths this newest weasel word to the lexicon of American political corruption."[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-charlesk-113)[Robert Conrad Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_J._Conrad "Robert J. Conrad") was the head of a Justice Department task force appointed by [Attorney General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Attorney_General "United States Attorney General")[Janet Reno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Reno "Janet Reno") to investigate Gore's fund-raising controversies. In the spring of 2000, Conrad asked Reno to appoint an [independent counsel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_counsel "Independent counsel") to continue the investigation. After looking into the matter, Reno judged that the appointment of an independent counsel was unwarranted.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-lehrer1-114)

During the 1990s, Gore spoke out on a number of issues. In a 1992 speech on the [Gulf War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War "Gulf War"), Gore stated that he twice attempted to get the U.S. government to pull the plug on support to [Saddam Hussein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein "Saddam Hussein"), citing Hussein's use of poison gas, support of terrorism, and his burgeoning nuclear program, but was opposed both times by the Reagan and Bush administrations.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-92speech2-115) In 1998, at a conference of [APEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APEC "APEC") hosted by [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia"), Gore objected to the indictment, arrest and jailing of Prime Minister [Mahathir Mohamad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahathir_Mohamad "Mahathir Mohamad")'s longtime second-in-command [Anwar Ibrahim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anwar_Ibrahim "Anwar Ibrahim"), a move which received a negative response from leaders there.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-APEC-116) Ten years later, Gore again protested when Ibrahim was arrested a second time,[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-summons-117) a decision condemned by Malaysian foreign minister Datuk Seri Dr [Rais Yatim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rais_Yatim "Rais Yatim").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-summons-117)

1996 electoral vote results. The Clinton-Gore ticket won 379–159.

In the 1996 presidential election, Clinton and Gore both ran for re-election for president and vice-president. They faced Republican Senate Majority Leader [Bob Dole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dole "Bob Dole"), with his running mate, [Jack Kemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Kemp "Jack Kemp"), a former member of House republican leadership and George H. W. Bush's secretary of Housing and Urban Development. Gore and Kemp debated once, in one of the lowest rated debates in history. Gore held his own against Kemp, and kept President Clinton's large lead against Dole stable. On November 5, 1996, Clinton and Gore were re-elected as president and vice-president with 379 electoral votes and an 8% margin of victory in the popular vote.

Soon afterward, Gore also had to contend with the [Clinton–Lewinsky scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton%E2%80%93Lewinsky_scandal "Clinton–Lewinsky scandal"), which involved an affair between President Clinton and a White House intern, [Monica Lewinsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monica_Lewinsky "Monica Lewinsky"). Gore initially defended Clinton, whom he believed to be innocent, stating: "He is the president of the country! He is my friend ... I want to ask you now, every single one of you, to join me in supporting him."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-biosen-32) After [Clinton was impeached](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_of_Bill_Clinton "Impeachment of Bill Clinton"), Gore continued to defend him, stating: "I've defined my job in exactly the same way for six years now ... to do everything I can to help him be the best president possible."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-biosen-32)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-vanityfair.com-87)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-politico.com-88)

## 2000 presidential campaign

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/Algoreexecmanchester.jpg/250px-Algoreexecmanchester.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Algoreexecmanchester.jpg)

In [Manchester, New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester,_New_Hampshire "Manchester, New Hampshire"), campaigning for President of the United States in 2000

During a speech that he gave on June 16, 1999, in [Carthage, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carthage,_Tennessee "Carthage, Tennessee"), Gore formally announced his candidacy for president. His major theme was the need to strengthen the American family.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-announce2000-118) He was introduced by his eldest daughter, [Karenna Gore Schiff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karenna_Gore_Schiff "Karenna Gore Schiff").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-announce2000-118) In making the speech, Gore also distanced himself from Bill Clinton, who he stated had lied to him.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-announce2000-118) Gore was "briefly interrupted" by [AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS "HIV/AIDS") protesters claiming Gore was working with the pharmaceutical industry to prevent access to generic medicines for poor nations and chanting "Gore's greed kills".[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-announce2000-118) Additional speeches were also interrupted by the protesters. Gore responded: "I love this country. I love the [First Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "First Amendment to the United States Constitution") ... Let me say in response to those who may have chosen an inappropriate way to make their point, that actually the crisis of AIDS in Africa is one that should command the attention of people in the United States and around the world." Gore also issued a statement saying that he supported efforts to lower the cost of the AIDS drugs, provided that they "are done in a way consistent with international agreements".[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-protestAIDS-119)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-briefing-120)

While Bill Clinton's job-approval ratings were around 60%, an April 1999 study by the [Pew Research Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pew_Research_Center "Pew Research Center") for the People found that respondents suffered from "Clinton fatigue" where they were "tired of all the problems associated with the Clinton administration" including the Lewinsky scandal and impeachment. Texas Governor and likely Republican presidential nominee [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush") was leading Gore 54% to 41% in polls during that time. Gore's advisers believed that the "Lewinsky scandal and Bill's past womanizing...alienated independent voters—especially the [soccer moms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soccer_mom "Soccer mom"), who stood for [traditional values](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_conservatism "Social conservatism")". Consequently, Gore's presidential campaign "veered too far in differentiating himself from Bill and his record and had difficulty taking advantage of the Clinton administration's legitimate successes". In addition, Hillary's candidacy for the open Senate seat in New York exacerbated the "three-way tensions evident in the White House since 1993", as "not only was Hillary unavailable as a campaigner, she was poaching top Democratic fund-raisers and donors who would normally concentrate on the vice president". In one instance "Hillary insisted on being invited [to a Los Angeles fundraiser for the vice president]—over the objections of the event's organizers", where the First Lady "shocked the vice president's supporters by soliciting donations for herself in front of Tipper".[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-vanityfair.com-87)

Gore faced an early challenge by former New Jersey senator [Bill Bradley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Bradley "Bill Bradley").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-announce2000-118) Bradley was the only candidate to oppose Gore and was considered a "fresh face" for the White House.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-boyhoodhome-121)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-polls99-122) Gore challenged Bradley to a series of debates which took the form of "town hall" meetings.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-townhall-123) Gore went on the offensive during these debates leading to a drop in the polls for Bradley.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-swing-124)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-clock-125) In the Iowa caucus the unions pledged their support to Gore, despite Bradley spending heavily in that state, and Bradley was much embarrassed by his two to one defeat there. Gore went on to capture the New Hampshire primary 53-47%, which had been a must-win state for Bradley. Gore then swept all of the primaries on Super Tuesday while Bradley finished a distant second in each state. On March 9, 2000, after failing to win any of the first 20 primaries and caucuses in the election process, Bradley withdrew his campaign and endorsed Gore. Gore eventually went on to win every primary and caucus and, in March 2000 even won the first primary election ever held over the Internet, the Arizona Presidential Primary.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-arizona-126) By then, he secured the Democratic nomination.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-dropout-127) As of 2023, Al Gore remains the only presidential candidate in American history who was not the incumbent president to win every single contest in his or her party primary.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Gore_Lieberman_2000_logo.svg/250px-Gore_Lieberman_2000_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gore_Lieberman_2000_logo.svg)

The logo for Gore and [Joe Lieberman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Lieberman "Joe Lieberman")'s campaign

On August 13, 2000, Gore announced that he had selected Senator [Joe Lieberman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Lieberman "Joe Lieberman") of Connecticut as his vice presidential running mate. Lieberman became "the first person of the [Jewish faith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaism "Judaism") to run for the nation's second-highest office". Many pundits saw Gore's choice of Lieberman as further distancing him from the scandals of the Clinton White House.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-chooses-128) Gore's daughter, Karenna, together with her father's former Harvard roommate [Tommy Lee Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Lee_Jones "Tommy Lee Jones"),[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-speak-129) officially nominated Gore as the Democratic presidential candidate during the [2000 Democratic National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Democratic_National_Convention "2000 Democratic National Convention") in Los Angeles, California.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-nominate-130) Gore accepted his party's nomination and spoke about the major themes of his campaign, stating in particular his plan to extend [Medicare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicare_(United_States) "Medicare (United States)") to pay for [prescription drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prescription_drugs "Prescription drugs") and to work for a sensible [universal health-care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_health_care "Universal health care") system.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-nominate-130) Soon after the convention, Gore hit the campaign trail with running mate Joe Lieberman. Gore and Bush were deadlocked in the polls.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-kickoff-131) They participated in three televised debates. While both sides claimed victory after each, Gore was critiqued as either too stiff, too reticent, or too aggressive in contrast to Bush.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-autogenerated4-132)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-eludes-133)

**Albert Arnold****Gore Jr.** (born March 31, 1948) is an American former politician, businessman, and environmentalist who served as the 45th [vice president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president_of_the_United_States "Vice president of the United States") from 1993 to 2001 under President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton"). A member of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"), he previously represented [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee") in both houses of the [U.S. Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Congress "U.S. Congress"), first as a member of the [U.S. House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_of_Representatives "U.S. House of Representatives") from 1977 to 1985, and then as a [U.S. senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._senator "U.S. senator") from 1985 to 1993. Gore was the Democratic nominee in the [2000 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election "2000 United States presidential election"), losing to [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") nominee [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush").

The son of politician [Albert Gore Sr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Gore_Sr. "Albert Gore Sr."), Gore was raised in Tennessee and [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), where he was born. After graduating from [Harvard University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University") and serving in the [U.S. Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Army "U.S. Army"), he quit law school to run as a representative for [Tennessee's 4th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee's_4th_congressional_district "Tennessee's 4th congressional district") in 1976. Gore was re-elected three times before running for U.S. Senate in [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_United_States_Senate_election_in_Tennessee "1984 United States Senate election in Tennessee"), winning re-election in [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_United_States_Senate_election_in_Tennessee "1990 United States Senate election in Tennessee"). He was considered a [moderate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Democrats_(United_States) "New Democrats (United States)") and an "[Atari Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atari_Democrat "Atari Democrat")". [Gore served as vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_presidency_of_Al_Gore "Vice presidency of Al Gore") during the [Clinton administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_administration "Clinton administration") from 1993 to 2001, defeating then-incumbents [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") and [Dan Quayle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Quayle "Dan Quayle") in [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_States_presidential_election "1992 United States presidential election"), and [Bob Dole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dole "Bob Dole") and [Jack Kemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Kemp "Jack Kemp") in [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_United_States_presidential_election "1996 United States presidential election"), and was the first Democrat to serve two full terms as vice president since [John Nance Garner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Nance_Garner "John Nance Garner"). As of 2025[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Al_Gore&action=edit), Gore's 1990 re-election remains the last time Democrats won a Senate election in Tennessee.

Gore was the Democratic presidential nominee in the 2000 election, in which he lost the [U.S. Electoral College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Electoral_College "U.S. Electoral College") vote by five electoral votes to [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") nominee George W. Bush while winning the [popular vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_vote "Popular vote") by 543,895 votes.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-ouregvp-2) The election concluded after the [U.S. Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Supreme_Court "U.S. Supreme Court") ruled 5–4 in _[Bush v. Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush\_v.\_Gore "Bush v. Gore")_ against a previous ruling by the [Supreme Court of Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Florida "Supreme Court of Florida") on a [re-count](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election_recount_in_Florida "2000 United States presidential election recount in Florida"). He is one of [five presidential candidates in American history to lose a presidential election despite winning the popular vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_presidential_elections_in_which_the_winner_lost_the_popular_vote "List of United States presidential elections in which the winner lost the popular vote").

After his vice presidency ended in 2001, Gore remained prominent as an author and [environmental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_activism_of_Al_Gore "Environmental activism of Al Gore") activist, and his work in [climate change activism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_activism "Climate change activism") earned him (jointly with the [IPCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPCC "IPCC")) the [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") in [2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Nobel_Peace_Prize "2007 Nobel Peace Prize"). Gore is the founder and chair of [The Climate Reality Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Climate_Reality_Project "The Climate Reality Project"), the co-founder and chair of [Generation Investment Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generation_Investment_Management "Generation Investment Management"), the since-defunct [Current TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Current_TV "Current TV") network, a former member of the Board of Directors of [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") and a senior adviser to Google.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-bio-3) Gore is also a partner in the [venture capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_capital "Venture capital") firm [Kleiner Perkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kleiner_Perkins "Kleiner Perkins"), heading its climate change solutions group.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-greenbusiness-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-partnerbio-5) He has served as a visiting professor at [Middle Tennessee State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Tennessee_State_University "Middle Tennessee State University"), [Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University_Graduate_School_of_Journalism "Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism"), [Fisk University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisk_University "Fisk University"), and the [University of California, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Los_Angeles "University of California, Los Angeles").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-bio-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-columbia-6)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-Fisk-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-UCLA-8) He served on the Board of Directors of [World Resources Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Resources_Institute "World Resources Institute").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-9)

Gore has received a number of awards that include the Nobel Peace Prize (joint award with the [Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intergovernmental_Panel_on_Climate_Change "Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change"), 2007), a [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award") for Current TV (2007), and a [Webby Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Webby_Award_winners#2005 "List of Webby Award winners") (2005). Gore was also the subject of the [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Documentary_Feature "Academy Award for Documentary Feature") winning (2007) documentary _[An Inconvenient Truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_Inconvenient\_Truth "An Inconvenient Truth")_ in 2006, as well as its 2017 sequel _[An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_Inconvenient\_Sequel:\_Truth\_to\_Power "An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power")_. In 2007, he was named a runner-up for _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_'s[2007 Person of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Person_of_the_Year "Time Person of the Year").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-Timeperson-10) In 2008, Gore won the [Dan David Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_David_Prize "Dan David Prize") for Social Responsibility,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-12) and in 2024 was awarded the [Presidential Medal of Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom "Presidential Medal of Freedom") by President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore#cite_note-13)
