[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Norske_nobelinstiutt_1.jpg/250px-Norske_nobelinstiutt_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Norske_nobelinstiutt_1.jpg)

The Norwegian Nobel Institute assists the Norwegian Nobel Committee in selecting recipients of the Nobel Peace Prize and in organising the annual award in Oslo.

The [Norwegian Nobel Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Nobel_Committee "Norwegian Nobel Committee") awards the [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") annually "to the person who shall have done the most or the best work for fraternity between nations, for the abolition or reduction of standing armies and for the holding and promotion of peace congresses."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-1) As dictated by [Alfred Nobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel")'s will, the award is administered by the [Norwegian Nobel Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Nobel_Committee "Norwegian Nobel Committee") and awarded by a committee of five people elected by the [Parliament of Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Norway "Parliament of Norway").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-2)

Each recipient receives a medal, a [diploma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diploma "Diploma"), and a monetary award prize (that has varied throughout the years).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-3) It is one of the five prizes established by the 1895 [will](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_(law) "Will (law)") of [Alfred Nobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel") (who died in 1896), awarded for outstanding contributions in [chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry"), [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics"), [literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature"), [physiology or medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-4)

## Overview

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Overview")]

The Peace Prize is presented annually in [Oslo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo "Oslo"), in the presence of the [King of Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Norway "King of Norway"), on 10 December, the anniversary of Nobel's death, and is the only Nobel Prize not presented in [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-5) Unlike the other prizes, the Peace Prize is occasionally awarded to an organisation (such as the [International Committee of the Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Committee_of_the_Red_Cross "International Committee of the Red Cross"), a three-time recipient) rather than an individual.

The Nobel Peace Prize was first awarded in 1901 to [Frédéric Passy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%A9d%C3%A9ric_Passy "Frédéric Passy") and [Henry Dunant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Dunant "Henry Dunant"), who shared a prize of 150,782 [Swedish kronor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_kronor "Swedish kronor") (equal to 7,731,004 kronor in 2008), and most recently in 2025 to [María Corina Machado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADa_Corina_Machado "María Corina Machado").

*   [Linus Pauling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linus_Pauling "Linus Pauling"), the Nobel Peace Prize laureate in 1962, is the only person to have been awarded two unshared Nobel Prizes; he won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1954.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-NobelFacts-6)
*   At 17 years of age, [Malala Yousafzai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malala_Yousafzai "Malala Yousafzai"), the 2014 recipient, is the youngest to be awarded the Peace Prize.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-NobelFacts-6)
*   The first woman to receive a Nobel Peace Prize was [Bertha von Suttner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertha_von_Suttner "Bertha von Suttner") in 1905. Of the 113 individual Nobel Peace Prize Laureates, 20 have been women.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-NobelFacts-6)
*   The [International Committee of the Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Committee_of_the_Red_Cross "International Committee of the Red Cross") has received the most Nobel Peace Prizes, having been awarded the Prize three times for its humanitarian work.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-NobelFacts-6)
*   Five Nobel Peace Prize Laureates were under arrest at the time of their awards: [Carl von Ossietzky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_von_Ossietzky "Carl von Ossietzky") (in 1935), [Aung San Suu Kyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aung_San_Suu_Kyi "Aung San Suu Kyi") (in 1991), [Liu Xiaobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Xiaobo "Liu Xiaobo") (in 2010), [Ales Bialiatski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ales_Bialiatski "Ales Bialiatski") (in 2022), and [Narges Mohammadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narges_Mohammadi "Narges Mohammadi") (in 2023).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-NobelFacts-6)

## Laureates

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Laureates")]

As of 2025[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates&action=edit), the Peace Prize has been awarded to 114 individuals and 28 organizations. Twenty women have won the Nobel Peace Prize, more than any other Nobel Prize.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-7) Only two recipients have won multiple Peace Prizes: the [International Committee of the Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Committee_of_the_Red_Cross "International Committee of the Red Cross") has won three times (1917, 1944 and 1963) and the [Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_High_Commissioner_for_Refugees "United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees") has won twice (1954 and 1981).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates#cite_note-NobelFacts-6) There have been 19 years in which the Peace Prize was not awarded.
